title: [GMCP 203.007.04] Adversarial and failure behavior: Transport adapter SPI and embedded/in-process operation
goal: Requirement GMCP-203-007-04. Close validation, authorization, isolation, privacy, bounded-resource, cancellation, concurrency, crash, retry, rollback, and recovery behavior. Add deterministic negative, attack, race, corruption, and fault-injection fixtures derived from the vector threat model. Vector outcome: A stable transport SPI admits in-process, Unix-domain socket, named-pipe, WebSocket or future transports without changing protocol semantics. A common conformance harness proves ordering, cancellation, limits, identity propagation, observability, shutdown, and error equivalence across adapters, while experimental transports are capability-negotiated and never silently presented as standard MCP. Done means production-path tests and retained evidence prove this work package; task closure or roadmap wording alone is not evidence.
